summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, mechanical aortic valve replacement, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for chest pain and shortness of breath. Her symptoms were attributed to a type II non-ST elevation myocardial infarction in the setting of fluid overload and demand ischemia. Troponins were mildly elevated but stable, with no acute EKG changes. She underwent hemodialysis, which improved her respiratory symptoms. Her INR was supratherapeutic, likely due to interaction with levofloxacin, so warfarin was held during admission. She was discharged home with services after clinical improvement, with instructions to follow up on INR testing, restart warfarin based on results, and use nitroglycerin for any recurrent chest pain.
